The average daily traffic for I-94 at Grange Avenue in 1972 when the noise measurements were taken was approximately 61,000 vehicles. The average daily traffic at the same location for the first six months of 1974 showed no increase because of the energy crisis. Under normal growth patterns we would expect a 3% increase. The study is therefore valid from the standpoint that neither traffic volumes nor noise levels have changed since 1972.
The health, welfare, and safety of the children at Hamlin-Garland School should be considered since increasing noise levels will interfer with the educational process in the classroom. Noise and air pollution will also be a factor to those living near the Airport Spur.
See pages 141 and 150 for a response.
Suggested College Avenue as an alternate to the Airport Spur.
See pages 79 and 80 for a response
Stated he introduced an assembly bill patterned after California law that would require the indoor noise levels be 50 dBA or less in a school after a freeway is built next do it.
Until legislation is enacted we will comply with current FHWA standards requiring 55 dBA interior levels.
Some have suggested that Bong Field or some place south or west of Milwaukee be used to replace Mitchell Field.
Refer to letter M-2 on page 194.
Representative Plewa has also commented by letter on the Draft EIS. His letter as well as a response are on pages 179 thru 181.
